response.text:
The settlement math is inverted, coupons are only partly applied, and several ordinary inputs crash checkout.

1. Tier “discount” is used as the amount charged, not the amount taken off. `total_amount * discount / 100` is the discount slice itself; the coupon is then subtracted from that slice. On a 100-unit standard basket the function computes `20 - coupon`, not `80 - coupon`. The first call returns `-10`; the second returns `0`. Premium is the same bug with 30. Customers are undercharged; the business loses the sale price; billing can record a credit instead of a charge.

2. The result is not floored at zero. A coupon larger than that slice yields a negative amount owed (first call: `-10`). Customers can be credited; payment or ledger code that rejects negatives fails the order.

3. Only `coupon_codes[0]` is read, despite the name `coupon_sum`. Later codes are silently ignored. Customers who pass more than one code do not get them; nothing tells them the extras were dropped.

4. An unknown code raises `KeyError`. The third call (`"NOPE"`) crashes instead of rejecting the coupon. That customer cannot check out; the caller gets an unhandled exception.

5. An empty `coupon_codes` list raises `IndexError` on `[0]`. Customers with no coupon cannot settle.

6. An unknown `account_tier` raises `KeyError` on `DISCOUNT_BY_TIER`. Anyone not exactly `"standard"` or `"premium"` cannot settle.

7. Money is computed with binary floats and no rounding to the minor unit. Non-round baskets can be off by fractions of a cent. Customers and reconciliation both see drift.
